text:
jamie: Heads-up — after d7224 merged into runtime we're seeing a 6-12% p99 tail latency bump on the small-chat canary A cohort. Traces point at kernel selection CPU overhead during token generation.

sahil: Saw that too, nice catch. Is this only on short sequences?

jamie: Mostly <128 tokens. Longer sequences look fine. KV cache hit rate unchanged, so not cache misses.

ana: (perf-bot): Canary rollout job 1851239800 started for runtime/d7224. Metrics window open.

ana: I ran a quick flame graph — the scheduler spends more time in kernel_probe() and in the decision tree for kernel choice. Looks like the new heuristics added an extra scan per request.

mike: Can we toggle kernel-autoselect off on the canary to confirm? There was a refactor that moved heuristics earlier in the pipeline.

jamie: Yes, propose: A/B canary with autoselect=false (control) vs autoselect=true (candidate). If control p99 < candidate p99 by >4% for 5m, abort and bisect.

olivia: I worry about noisy short windows. Suggest window=10m and require sustained gap across 3 consecutive 1m subwindows. Also avoid instant auto-rollback for single spike.

perf-bot: Perf regression alert: p99 +9% (small-chat, 5m) — threshold exceeded.

jamie: OK plan: pause canary rollout, flip autoselect=false on canary nodes, re-run A/B with identical traffic split and synthetic trial traffic. If that removes the regression we can bisect commits in that feature stack.

sahil: For bisect: start by disabling the heuristics change (PR #1287) locally then progressively re-enable smaller hunks. If repro is flaky, run nightly bench with `scripts/bench/canary-run --workload small-chat --iters 2000 --trace` and collect cpu profiles.

mike: Also add a KV-cache stress: short TTLs to simulate churn — we saw heuristics do extra kernel checks when KV entries rotate. Include `--kv-ttl-ms 2000` in bench.

jamie: Good call. I'll create a temporary gating rule in the rollout pipeline: canary.guardrails.perf.slo.p99 <= baseline*1.04 and canary.guardrails.min_window=600s and canary.guardrails.consecutive_buckets=3. If violated -> auto-pause (not auto-revert) so humans can confirm.

olivia: I think we should auto-revert for critical regressions (p99 > +10% for 10m) but for smaller deltas auto-pause only. Flapping is real if we auto-revert too aggressively.

jamie: Agreed. New behavior: auto-pause at +4% sustained; auto-revert only at +10% sustained or if throughput drops >5%. We'll add cooldown 15m to avoid churn.

perf-bot: Action items: 1) run bench with autoselect=false vs true (jamie) 2) run KV stress bench (mike) 3) create rollout guardrail change PR (jamie/olivia) 4) start bisect checklist if toggle confirms (sahil).

jamie: I'll open the PR for guardrail changes and flip the canary flag now. Pushing to canary nodes...

deploy-bot: Canary flag flip deployed to canary group (nodes: canary-7, canary-8) — id: deploy-1851239905

mike: Bench running: `scripts/bench/canary-run --workload small-chat --iters 2000 --kv-ttl-ms 2000 --trace` — ETA ~12m.

jamie: Early numbers: control (autoselect=false) p99 118ms, candidate p99 128ms over first 3m. That's ~8% gap replicating the issue.

sahil: Good reproduction. Start git bisect on the runtime branch. Start point: HEAD@{d7224}, good: HEAD~5 before heuristics refactor. Bisect script: `tools/perf/bisect.sh --bench small-chat --iters 1000 --metric p99 --threshold 1.03`.

olivia: Add a telemetry tag to bisect runs so we can trace which commit introduced extra kernel calls. `--trace-tag canary-d7224`

jamie: Running bisect now. If bisect narrows to the heuristics refactor commit, we'll split out the scanning pass into cached decisions to avoid per-request scans.

perf-bot: CI perf job queued: ci/perf/small-chat/1851239930. Will compare against baseline.

mike: One more note — we should add a runtime config to limit kernel selection CPU budget per request: `max_kernel_choice_cycles=2000` fallback to default kernel if exceeded. That would act as a soft-guard.

jamie: Good defensive knob. Add to PR as feature-flagged. We'll telemetry any fallback activations.

sahil: If bisect points to a dependency change (eg new kernel metadata parsing lib), escalate to eng-runtime infra owners.

jamie: Update: bisect reports commit 0af9c2 introduced the regression — it moved the heuristics earlier and added an unordered map scan. Revert patching shows p99 back to baseline.

olivia: Sounds like revert + rework. Let's revert on canary, run a longer 1h canary test with KV stress. If stable, promote and then open a follow-up PR that reintroduces heuristics but caches kernel choices per-request-prefix.

jamie: I'll push the revert to canary and keep guardrails in place. After promote we'll also add the `max_kernel_choice_cycles` safety knob.

deploy-bot: Revert deployed to canary (deploy-1851239958). Canary guardrails remain active.

jamie: Thanks all. Follow-ups: I'll post the bisect logs and flame graphs in the thread and create the guardrail PR. If anyone wants access to perf runs, ping me. :thumbsup:

olivia: Thanks — good triage.

mike: Nice work everyone.

perf-bot: Thread closed after revert confirmation.
